newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Platform for Australia Wandoo oil field completed.
newsitem.headline: Platform for Australia Wandoo oil field completed.

text.p: Far East Levingston Shipbuilding Ltd (FELS) said on Thursday it had completed building a 6,200-ton offshore production rig for Australia's Wandoo oil field.
The rig will be positioned early next year at the field offshore western Australia to increase production to 40,000 barrels per day (bpd), the company said in a statement.
Current production is about 10,000 bpd, industry sources said.

The Wandoo field has recoverable reserves of about 75 million barrels and is operated by Australia's Ampolex Ltd. Mobil Corp of the United States took contol of Ampolex recently following a hostile takeover.
The field produces a heavy crude with an American Petroleum Institute gravity of 19.4 percent.
The production rig is being towed to Australia from Singapore shipyards so it can be hooked-up to a concrete substructure at the oil field.
FELS, part of the Keppel Group, said commissioning would take place in February 1997.
The production unit has a storage capacity of 400,000 barrels.
Keppel is part of the Wandoo Alliance, a group of contractors who are developing the field at a cost of Australian $480 million.
